findings.label: Verifier hardening is unpushed, so the branch of record verifies less
findings.detail: 8a48e5f9 is local-only (HEAD 4 ahead / 0 behind origin/stack; the other three ahead-commits belong to other sessions). origin/stack's scripts/provision_checkout.py DOES carry the IAM narrowing that blocked the previous pass - route_statement_id, a per-route source_arn and live_policy_statements inside verify(), read off the branch - so unlike last time the code of record cannot re-widen anything. What is missing on the remote is verifier strength: no live-artifact scoping (the grant report reasons over a local export), WIX_SITE_ID omitted from the hand-enumerated env key list, and exit 0 on gate-off-with-readiness-set. --verify is what an operator runs before enabling initiation, so the remote copy would report success in the one state the evidence calls the point where inertness ends.

findings.label: The new gate-contract tests read the shared working tree and skip when the handler is absent
findings.detail: tests/test_checkout_gate_contract.py resolves the handler as ROOT / amplify/functions/ecommerce/checkout/handler.py and does pytest.skip('checkout handler not present in this checkout'). The same commit fixed exactly these two shapes elsewhere: it asserted presence before parsing in test_no_float_arithmetic_on_the_money_path ('a money module that is not in the package is the more serious defect, not the excuse to skip the check') and parametrised two property tests over a `committed` fixture built from git archive HEAD precisely because the working tree carries other sessions' uncommitted edits. The handler is not on this task's owned paths, so it is the file most likely to be changed by another session, and these five assertions are the pinning mechanism for the substituted deliverable. Latent today: the handler is clean, identical at HEAD and origin/stack, its line numbers match the live-measured snapshot exactly (229/233/259/290/312/323), and the file passes (5 passed, run as a narrow spot-check).
findings.action: Parametrise the gate-contract assertions over the committed fixture as well, and assert the handler is present instead of skipping.

findings.detail: wecare-checkout:live is v2, CodeSha256 1Ho3NbcbR3mlX8n3UBVth0wSSnBqh5OXPb1r1XETMHM=, published 13:49:45Z by a concurrent session and matching none of the three packages reproducible from this tree. What remains unrecorded is which revision produced it, which is a chain-of-custody gap on a payment-path function and is not this coder's to close.

findings.label: wecare-razorpay-webhook is v46, not the v45 the brief named
findings.detail: Measured v45 before and after by this task, then moved to v46 at 14:12:34Z by another session. Attribution is evidenced three ways: CloudTrail shows five functions' code replaced in the window and none is wecare-checkout; scripts/provision_checkout.py contains zero occurrences of 'razorpay-webhook' and exactly one publish_version call, inside ensure_live_alias keyed on FUNCTION_NAME = wecare-checkout; and the only invocation this iteration was --verify, which returns before reaching any ensure_* function. The shared IAM user cannot discriminate sessions and the document says so rather than claiming it can. Rolling the alias back would revert another session's deployed payment-webhook fix. The condition's purpose - that this task moves no existing function's alias - holds and is evidenced across five spot-checked functions.
findings.action: None for this task. Treat the brief's literal v45 condition as unsatisfiable and do not roll back.

findings.label: PAYMENT_INITIATION_DISABLED was never observed live; owner acceptance of the substitution is NOT EVIDENCED
findings.detail: The create probe returns 401, not the literal PAYMENT_INITIATION_DISABLED the brief named. It is structurally unreachable: require_customer runs before the body is parsed (lines 229 vs 233) and inside _create payment_readiness is evaluated before the gate (277 vs 323), so with both EXPECTED_* empty an authenticated request gets 409 payment_unavailable. Making it observable requires weakening authentication or minting a customer token, neither authorised. The previous pass's complaint was provenance, not the trade: 'owner, 2026-10-01' was cited inside the document making the claim. That citation is withdrawn and replaced by docs/execution/snapshots/checkout-gate-ordering-20261001.json, measured from the live alias's bytes and stating ownerAcceptance NOT EVIDENCED in the artifact itself, plus tests/test_checkout_gate_contract.py (5 assertions) and tests/test_checkout_handler.py::test_create_disabled_prepares_attempt_but_sends_nothing_and_makes_no_order with an authenticated fixture asserting 59900 integer paise, INR, one attempt row, a PAYREF# reservation and no order keys. That is the honest resolution; it records a measurement without manufacturing a sign-off.
findings.action: Owner to accept the substitution explicitly, or authorise a customer token plus readiness values for a live observation. Not coder work.

findings.label: _package_of has an if/else whose branches are identical
findings.detail: `return parts[:-1] if parts[-1] != "__init__.py" else parts[:-1]`. Both arms are correct, because a package's __init__.py has that package as its containing directory, so the distinction the docstring describes needs no branch. The hazard is a future reader seeing an if/else that must mean something and 'correcting' the dead branch to parts[:-2], which would make every relative import from an __init__.py resolve one level too high. Bounded: test_relative_import_resolution_cases pins resolve('lambda_utils/ecommerce/__init__.py', 'money', 1) == 'lambda_utils.ecommerce.money', so such an edit fails rather than shipping.
findings.action: Collapse to `return parts[:-1]` and keep the docstring explaining why no branch is needed.

findings.label: The presigned-URL guard is narrower than its claim, and the fetch does not check the URL scheme
findings.detail: get_function returns a short-lived presigned S3 URL carrying an X-Amz-Signature, which is credential-shaped material. live_members handles it correctly today: fetched in-process, never printed, never passed as an argument, and kept out of the download-failure message, which uses type(exc).__name__; scripts/provision_checkout.py has zero logger references, so there is no logging expression to leak through. But test_the_presigned_download_url_is_never_printed_or_stored inspects only print calls plus the `except Exception` return region, while its docstring claims 'a log line, an argument or any logging expression' - adding a logger would not be caught. Separately, live_members calls urllib.request.urlopen(location) with `# noqa: S310` suppressing the lint that exists for exactly this, with no check that location starts with https://.
findings.action: Widen the walk beyond print to any call taking the location, and add an https scheme check before urlopen.
